children: LGI Homes entered into a Seventh Amendment to its revolving credit agreement to enhance liquidity and extend maturities. The amendment provides approximately $1.166 billion in aggregate revolving commitments, includes a $175 million incremental facility, and updates borrowing base values and certain covenants. Commitments now mature on a staggered schedule, with most extending to October 9, 2030. The company expects the amendment to support growth and general corporate needs.
: Wells Fargo Bank, as administrative agent, and other lenders
: Extend maturities and increase liquidity for growth
